text:
Simon: Heads-up: short proposal for a slimline streaming handshake + resumable tokens to reduce edge memory pressure and simplify proxy state. patch/diagram incoming.
Jena: curious — how is this different from the resume-token work from last year?
Simon: key differences: token is stateless and verifiable by upstream (no long-lived session store in the proxy), much shorter TTL, and explicit offset + checksum so we can cheaply validate resumes. goal is to avoid per-stream heap retention.
Arpit: sketch the flow please.
Simon: flow sketch: client sends initial stream request; gateway returns immediate accept (200 + header) with Resume-Token in response headers; gateway proxies upstream and streams through; if client disconnects it reconnects with ?resume=<token> and gateway validates token and resumes from offset by requesting upstream resume point.
Maya: what about hedging/fanout? if we retry to another backend the token must encode a monotonic offset and a checksum of the last committed chunk so different backends can validate/seek.
Simon: agreed — token = base64(json{model,route_id,offset,nonce,chunk_csum,exp}) signed by gateway KMS key. small and opaque to clients.
Jena: side-effects concern: if the model call triggers downstream writes, resume could replay them. how do we prevent that?
Simon: resume is only allowed for streaming-read operations. we will add a route-level flag allow_resume_for_side_effects=false by default. upstream can set header X-Resume-Allowed: true for specific idempotent endpoints. if side-effects detected, gateway emits X-Resume-Allowed: false and includes that in token metadata.
Arpit: metrics to add: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_reject_reason (expired|mismatch|side_effects), token_issued, token_revoked, token_replay_detected.
Maya: also add per-route histograms: resumed_latency_delta, bytes_saved_by_resume, resumed_partial_count. these help quantify win.
Simon: quick example config sketch for a gateway route: 
```
resume:
  enabled: true
  signing_kid: "gw-2026-03"
  max_offset_window: 1000000
  allow_side_effects: false
  token_ttl_secs: 120
```
Jena: billing interaction? if upstream counts tokens produced before the client reconnect, we need checkpoints so billing is accurate.
Simon: propose: upstream writes periodic checkpoint headers `X-Billing-Checkpoint: tokens=1234,nonce=abcd` which the gateway persists (or folds into the Resume-Token). on resume, gateway reconciles checkpoint to avoid double-billing.
Sara: +1 — I'll add evals to catch any truncated/resume-corrupted outputs.
deploy-bot: Heads-up: feature-flag branch `resume-proto` scheduled to deploy to staging tomorrow 09:00 UTC :rocket:
Simon: thanks — I'll open an RFC PR with diagrams, sequence diagrams for failure modes (network blips, hedged responders, partial commits), and a test plan.
Jena: nice. can we also simulate a backend that returns inconsistent checkpoints to ensure the gateway rejects bad tokens?
Simon: yes — test matrix will include inconsistent-checkpoint, truncated-chunk, and simultaneous-resume-race.
Maya: FYI we should add a short-lived debug endpoint to fetch token contents (admin-only) so ops can triage resume failures quickly.
Simon: good call. will include admin decode and required audit logging.
Sara: I'll add a small prompt set that forces midstream truncation cases.
Simon: ideal next step: RFC + prototype on staging behind flag. thanks all.
